IBM.rationale: IBM presents a moderately attractive fundamental case with meaningful near-term headwinds that cap the score. Pillar 1 (fundamentals): YoY trajectory is unambiguously positive — revenue +9.5%, EPS +14.3%, all margin tiers expanding, OCF +18.3%, ROE surging to 32.5%, and equity base growing 22.7% YoY. The software-led mix shift is working: Red Hat at 10% growth, OpenShift at $2B ARR, watsonx at $12B+ bookings. However, leverage remains high at 3.73x D/E, Q1 2026 GAAP operating margin of 8.7% is well below the trailing 15.3%, and consulting growth is soft. Pillar 2 (valuation): PE has collapsed from ~50x to 22x — near the floor of its 365-day range — while fundamentals materially improved. This is a genuine re-rating opportunity if earnings durability holds, though the 4.5% earnings yield barely exceeds the 4.46% 10Y Treasury, limiting deep-value appeal. Pillar 3 (catalyst): The Accenture guidance cut on June 18 triggered a sector selloff that dragged IBM down ~5.5%, creating a potential entry point if Q2 earnings (expected mid-July) confirm the Q1 trajectory. The $11B Confluent acquisition closing in mid-March and the z17 mainframe cycle (48% growth) provide near-term revenue tailwinds. However, the consulting headwind and enterprise AI deployment uncertainty (91% of executives don't understand AI dependencies per IBM's own study) temper catalyst conviction. Net: a sound franchise at a compressed multiple, but high leverage and near-term sector headwinds prevent a stronger score.
